pharm: Bacteriostatic antibiotic that inhibits bacterial protein synthesis by binding the 30S ribosomal subunit; broad activity against Gram-positive, Gram-negative, atypical and some protozoal organisms
quick: 250 mg QID or 500 mg BID (up to 500 mg QID severe)
Empty stomach, 1 h before or 2 h after food/dairy
Renal and hepatic function on prolonged use
summary: Tetracycline is a broad-spectrum bacteriostatic antibiotic that inhibits bacterial protein synthesis at the 30S ribosome. It is used for susceptible respiratory, genitourinary, rickettsial, chlamydial, mycoplasmal and skin infections, acne, and as part of Helicobacter pylori regimens. Absorption is impaired by food, dairy and di/trivalent cations (calcium, magnesium, aluminum, iron, zinc), so it is taken on an empty stomach. It is contraindicated in pregnancy, lactation and children under 8 years owing to permanent tooth discoloration and effects on bone growth. Photosensitivity, esophageal irritation and superinfection are notable adverse effects.
indications: Upper and lower respiratory tract infections caused by susceptible organisms
Rickettsial infections (Rocky Mountain spotted fever, typhus, Q fever)
Chlamydial and mycoplasmal infections (including atypical pneumonia, urethritis)
Brucellosis, cholera, plague, tularemia (with streptomycin where indicated)
Syphilis and other infections in penicillin-allergic patients

dosage.d: 250 mg four times daily or 500 mg twice daily
Up to 500 mg four times daily
500 mg twice daily initially, then taper to 125-500 mg/day
Continue therapy for at least 10 days
500 mg four times daily for 7 days

admin: Take on an empty stomach, at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after meals
Avoid dairy products, antacids and iron/zinc/calcium/magnesium supplements within 2-3 hours
Take with a full glass of water and remain upright to reduce esophageal irritation
Do not use expired tetracycline (risk of Fanconi-type syndrome from degradation products)
moa: Binds reversibly to the 30S ribosomal subunit of susceptible bacteria, blocking attachment of aminoacyl-tRNA to the mRNA-ribosome complex and thereby inhibiting bacterial protein synthesis; the effect is primarily bacteriostatic.
preg: Contraindicated. Use during the second half of pregnancy can cause permanent yellow-grey-brown tooth discoloration and enamel hypoplasia and may inhibit fetal bone growth; high doses have been associated with maternal hepatotoxicity.
lact: Contraindicated/avoid. Tetracyclines are excreted in breast milk; risk of dental staining and inhibition of bone growth in the infant (although milk calcium may limit absorption).
renal: Avoid or reduce dose; tetracycline (unlike doxycycline) is renally eliminated and accumulates in renal impairment. It has an anti-anabolic effect that can raise BUN; excessive accumulation may cause azotemia, hyperphosphatemia and acidosis.
hepatic: Use with caution; avoid high or prolonged dosing. Hepatotoxicity, including fatal fatty liver, has occurred, particularly in pregnancy, renal impairment and with high intravenous doses.

major: Oral retinoids (isotretinoin/acitretin) - increased intracranial hypertension risk
Penicillins - bacteriostatic tetracycline may antagonize bactericidal activity
moderate: Antacids / iron / calcium / magnesium / zinc / dairy - markedly reduced absorption (chelation)
Digoxin - increased levels in some patients
interactions.food: Food and dairy impair absorption; take on an empty stomach
interactions.diagnostics: May cause false elevations in urinary catecholamines and interfere with some glucose tests; can raise BUN

emergency: Raised intracranial pressure with vision loss

monitoring: Renal function (BUN, creatinine) on prolonged therapy
Signs of superinfection or C. difficile
counsel: Take on an empty stomach with a full glass of water and stay upright
Separate from milk, antacids, iron and calcium/magnesium supplements by 2-3 hours
Use sunscreen and avoid excess sun exposure
Do not use during pregnancy, breastfeeding or in young children
Complete the full course even if you feel better
pk: Antibacterial effect within hours; steady state in ~24-48 h
20-25 C, protect from light and moisture; do not use after expiry
pearls: Chelates di/trivalent cations - separate from dairy, antacids, iron and calcium
Avoid in pregnancy, lactation and children <=8 years (tooth/bone effects)
Outdated tetracycline can cause a reversible Fanconi-type renal tubular syndrome
Photosensitivity is common - counsel on sun protection
Renally excreted, so doxycycline is preferred in renal impairment
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered, then space remaining doses; if it is almost time for the next dose, skip it. Do not double up.
overdose: Acute overdose mainly causes gastrointestinal upset (nausea, vomiting). The principal serious risk with very high or intravenous dosing is hepatotoxicity, especially in pregnancy and renal impairment. Management is supportive; there is no specific antidote, and dialysis is not effective.
